new_scholarship.name: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
new_scholarship.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support postdoctoral researchers in the life sciences for up to two years, with international mobility between countries as a core condition of eligibility. In EMBC Member States EMBO grants the host institution funds so it can issue an employment contract to the fellow; fellows based outside EMBC Member States receive a stipend intended to cover living costs. The fellowship also carries a travel and relocation allowance, child daycare support for non-EMBC fellows, and access to EMBO Laboratory Leadership courses. Applications are accepted throughout the year, with hard cutoffs for each evaluation round.
new_scholarship.duration: Up to two years; minimum one year; maximum combined full-time and part-time duration 36 months
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications accepted throughout the year; next cutoff date / hard deadline Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET
new_scholarship.application_period: Rolling applications; evaluation rounds with hard cutoffs (next cutoff 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET)
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: PhD holders in the life sciences who obtained their doctorate within the two years before submitting the application, have at least one first-author publication (or verifiably peer-reviewed first-author preprint), and are applying to move to a different country than where the PhD was obtained.

Applicants must have at least one first author publication (research paper) accepted in or published in an international peer reviewed journal at the time of application
A first author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews obtained from an independent peer review service is also sufficient for eligibility
All applications must involve movement between countries
Applications to go to the country in which the PhD was obtained will not be considered

Candidates who have already started working in the host laboratory may apply only if they have been living in the host country for less than six months at the time the application is submitted
Candidates can submit only one application for one project at one host laboratory at each round of selection
Projects that are a direct continuation of the PhD work are not eligible

Travel and relocation allowance as a lump sum
Child daycare allowance up to EUR 2,500 per fellowship year per child for children under six (non-EMBC fellows only)

Effective from the Autumn 2026 selection round a host laboratory may support a maximum of one candidate per selection round. Effective from the Autumn 2027 selection round (applications submitted after 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET) re-applications will no longer be permitted.

programme_detail_official.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers throughout Europe and the world for a period of up to two years. International mobility is a key requirement. In EMBC Member States the fellowship takes the form of a grant to the host institution to cover an employment contract for the fellow; fellows in other countries receive a stipend. The fellowship includes a travel and relocation allowance and support for fellows with children, and awardees can attend an EMBO Laboratory Leadership course and become part of the global EMBO Fellows' Network.
programme_detail_official.coverage: EMBC Member States plus other countries worldwide; funding covers the fellow's salary or stipend and a travel and relocation allowance, and never tuition or institutional running costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your PhD was awarded within the two years before you submit
Secure at least one first-author publication, or a first-author preprint with verifiable in-depth peer review from an independent peer review service
Choose a host laboratory in a country other than where you obtained your PhD
Check the six-month rule: you cannot apply to a laboratory where you previously worked for more than six months in total, or to your PhD supervisor or PhD institution
Agree the start date with the host supervisor and confirm the host institution will issue an employment contract
Register and complete the application in the EMBO portal well before the hard cutoff of your chosen evaluation round
common_rejection_risks: PhD older than two years at the date of application, with no approved exception
No first-author peer-reviewed publication and no qualifying peer-reviewed preprint
Applying to the country where the PhD was obtained
Applying to the PhD host laboratory, department or supervisor, or to a former host laboratory where you worked for more than six months
Applying from inside the host country after living there more than six months
The proposed project being a direct continuation of the PhD work
Missing the hard cutoff for the evaluation round
More than one application in the same round, which is not permitted
Two candidates from the same host laboratory in one round from the Autumn 2026 round onwards
estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees, overheads and consumables are explicitly not covered and must be found by the host laboratory
National taxes and social contributions arrangements in the host country, which EMBO cannot advise on
Visa, travel and relocation costs beyond the EMBO travel and relocation lump sum
Any costs arising if the fellowship duration is shortened below two years
document_audit: First-author publication list matches the eligibility claim
Peer-review evidence for a preprint is verifiable through an independent peer review service, not individual comments or highlights
Host supervisor's name and host institution are stated and correct
CV and publication list are complete and consistent with the proposal
Proposal topic is not a continuation of the PhD work

alerts.message: Applications are accepted year-round but each evaluation round has a hard cutoff; the next one shown by EMBO is Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET. Late applications roll to the following round.

new_scholarship.name: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships
new_scholarship.description: The Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships scheme funds placements for working science journalists at research institutions and for life scientists seeking to move into full-time science journalism in media newsrooms. It is restricted to applicants resident in an EMBC Member State whose placements also take place in an EMBC Member State, in person. Successful applicants receive a daily subsistence stipend based on the cost of living in the host country, covering living expenses and travel. Applications are accepted at any time but must be registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 Central European Summer Time on 30 October each year.
new_scholarship.duration: Journalists: minimum three months, maximum six months. Researchers transitioning to journalism: minimum three months, maximum twelve months.
new_scholarship.deadline: 30 October each year, 23:59 Central European Summer Time (applications may be submitted at any time but must be registered by this deadline)
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications can be submitted at any time; selection takes place once a year and fully completed applications must be registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October each year. Applicants are notified by mid-November.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Either an employed or freelance working journalist with demonstrable relevant experience and samples of published or broadcast work who wants to deepen their science knowledge, or a life scientist with a master's degree or higher who wants to transition into full-time science journalism and has prior reporting on the life sciences.
eligibility: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State
The placement or placements must also occur in an EMBC Member State
Placements must be in person; virtual placements are not eligible
If Fellows undertake two or more placements, at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the others
Applicants are not subject to any age restriction
Journalists must demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation
Journalists must provide samples of their published or broadcast work
Journalists must show a genuine desire to broaden and deepen their knowledge of science, not a search for immediate publication opportunities
Life scientists seeking to transition to full-time journalism must hold a master's degree or higher, preferably in a life sciences discipline
Life scientists must demonstrate a genuine intention to move into journalism as a profession, with evidence of prior reporting on the life sciences or associated disciplines
Personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals are not accepted as evidence of prior journalism
Fellows are expected not to undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the fellowship term
coverage: Daily subsistence stipend sized to the cost of living in the host country
Travel costs connected with the placement
benefits: Daily stipend intended to cover living expenses and travel costs in the host country
Three to six months of funding for practising journalists
Three to twelve months of funding for researchers transitioning into science journalism

new_scholarship.english_requirement: The proposal and curriculum vitae must be in English; samples of journalism work may be in any language.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection takes place once a year, with outcomes notified by email by mid-November. Applicants are judged by the EMBO advisory board on the genuine desire to broaden science knowledge or to move into journalism, the quality of the proposal and the learning outcomes set. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Working science journalists based in EMBC Member States who want an in-person research sabbatical, and mid-career life scientists with a master's or doctorate who have already begun reporting and want to move into full-time science journalism in a mainstream newsroom.
new_scholarship.notes: The fellowship cannot be extended. Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes and other costs. Both the applicant and the placement must be in an EMBC Member State, so this scheme cannot be used from outside Europe or for a placement outside Europe.
new_scholarship.funding_duration: 3 to 6 months for journalists; 3 to 12 months for researchers transitioning to journalism

programme_detail_official.description: The scheme supports science journalism by providing journalists with funded placements (sabbaticals) at one or more research institutions to deepen and broaden their knowledge of the life and associated sciences, and by supporting researchers who wish to transition to full-time science journalism with funded placements in one or more media newsrooms. It was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
programme_detail_official.coverage: EMBC Member States for both applicant residence and placement; funding covers a daily subsistence stipend for living expenses and travel.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you reside in an EMBC Member State and that your placement will also be in an EMBC Member State
Decide whether you are applying as a practising journalist or as a researcher transitioning to journalism - the two tracks have different duration, evidence and proposal requirements
Identify and approach your host research institution or newsroom before submitting (formal written acceptance is not required at application, but the placement must be real)
Write a proposal of no more than three pages in English with specific learning and knowledge outcomes
Prepare your CV in English with permanent residential address, email and mobile number
Assemble samples of published or broadcast journalism work, which may be in any language
Submit through the EMBO application portal well before 23:59 CEST on 30 October
common_rejection_risks: Applicant resident outside an EMBC Member State, or proposing a placement outside an EMBC Member State
Proposing a virtual placement, which is explicitly not eligible
Taking two placements in the same EMBC Member State, when at least one must be in a different one
For researchers, applying without a master's degree or higher, or without a life sciences degree
Presenting only blog posts, social media posts, or academic commentary and reviews as evidence of prior journalism - these are explicitly excluded
A proposal over three pages, or not in English
Journalists seeking support for immediate publication opportunities rather than learning
Missing the 23:59 CEST 30 October portal registration deadline, since only fully completed applications are considered

alerts.message: Only fully completed applications registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 Central European Summer Time on 30 October are considered. The next deadline is 30 October 2026.
Both your residence and your placement must be in an EMBC Member State. Applicants based outside Europe cannot use this scheme.
Fellows must not take other work during the fellowship, and journalists must not report on their host institution while resident there.
The scholarship period cannot be extended, and periods beyond three months for researcher fellows are subject to ongoing assessment.

submission_workflow: Register on the EMBO application portal
Approach the proposed research institution (journalists) or newsroom (researchers) and agree the placement in person
Draft the three-page English proposal with specific learning outcomes
Prepare the English CV and journalism samples
Submit the complete application through the portal before 23:59 CEST on 30 October
Await the outcome, notified by email by mid-November
After a conditional offer, finalise the placement and obtain written confirmation from the host

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Official wording on the Eligibility page: 'Life scientists seeking support to transition into full time (science) journalism must have a master's degree or higher, and preferably in a life sciences discipline.' and 'Journalists must be able to demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation.' The Benefits page sets duration: 'For journalists, the duration of the fellowship is for a minimum of three months and a maximum of six months... For researchers wishing to become science journalists the duration of the fellowship is for a minimum of three months and a maximum of 12 months.'
